mainTopic: Whether בית דין can uproot a Torah law: impure תרומה, the ממזר child, and the minor wife (הפקר בית דין הפקר and מת מצוה).
overview: This amud continues the case of someone who separates impure produce as תרומה for pure produce. The גמרא compares it to a משנה about a perforated and a non-perforated pot. It answers that impure produce is full תרומה by Torah law, and proves this from רבי אלעאי's teaching about separating bad produce for good. רבה then challenges רב חסדא: how could the רבנן turn Torah-level תרומה back into ordinary food, when a בית דין cannot uproot a Torah law? רב חסדא tries to prove that בית דין can do this, first from the child of the first husband who is called a ממזר, and then from a ברייתא about a husband who inherits his minor wife and becomes impure for her. Each proof is pushed aside. The child is only made stricter. Inheritance is a money matter, covered by הפקר בית דין הפקר, which רבי יצחק and רבי אלעזר learn from פסוקים. The husband may become impure for her because she counts as a מת מצוה, since her father's family, who do not inherit her, will not come to bury her.

steps.title: Comparing to the perforated pot case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the separated impure portion counts as complete תרומה, when in a similar משנה the separated תרומה still needs תרומה and מעשר taken for it from elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from the משנה that says: if someone separates תרומה from produce grown in a perforated pot for produce grown in a non-perforated pot, his תרומה is תרומה, but it may not be eaten until he separates תרומה and מעשר for it from somewhere else?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that looks similar and asks why our case is treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pot case, the separated portion is תרומה, but it is not fully 'clean'. It still needs תרומה and מעשר taken for it. Yet in our case of impure produce, the separated portion is treated as complete תרומה with nothing more needed. So why the difference?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (introduces a contradiction between two cases)
A plant pot with a hole, treated like ground (the full Torah obligation of tithes)
A pot with no hole, where the obligation is only from the רבנן
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which is holy
A tithe (a tenth) taken from produce

phrases.english: In what way is it different from that which we learned in a משנה:
If one separates from produce of a perforated pot for produce of a non-perforated pot,
phrases.notes: A pot with a hole counts like the ground, so its produce must be tithed by Torah law. A pot without a hole only needs tithing because the רבנן said so.

phrases.english: his תרומה is תרומה,
but it may not be eaten until he separates on it
תרומה and tithe from another place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier view (from before this section) that the separated impure portion is fully תרומה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the separated impure portion is complete תרומה needing no further separation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a similar case (perforated pot for non-perforated pot), the separated תרומה still needs תרומה and מעשר taken for it. So why not here too?

steps.title: Impure produce is real תרומה by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that impure produce separated as תרומה is full תרומה by Torah law, following רבי אלעאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because by Torah law it is complete תרומה, following רבי אלעאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the impure case is different because by Torah law the separation fully works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pot case, the separation only partly works, so the separated portion still needs fixing. But separating from impure produce works completely by Torah law. Only the רבנן added a penalty, so the separated portion is complete תרומה. The source for this comes next, from רבי אלעאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different
By Torah law
Complete, proper, full-fledged

phrases.english: Here it is different,
for by Torah law it is full-fledged תרומה,
in accordance with רבי אלעאי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The impure case should be like the pot case, where the separated portion still needs תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Impure produce becomes full תרומה by Torah law, unlike the pot case.

steps.title: רבי אלעאי's verse: separating from bad produce for good
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי brings a פסוק to show that separating תרומה from lower-quality produce for better produce still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי said: How do we know that if someone separates תרומה from bad produce for good produce, his תרומה is תרומה? Because it is written: 'And you shall bear no sin because of it, when you set apart its best from it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes רבי אלעאי's teaching, which supports the answer in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says you will carry no sin when you give the best part. This suggests that giving a worse part is a sin. The next step explains why that proves the separation still works.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
The one who separates תרומה
From the bad (produce) for the good (produce)
Its best part (literally, its fat)

phrases.english: As רבי אלעאי said:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לַתּוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה
phrases.english: From where do we know that one who separates תרומה from the bad for the good
that his תרומה is תרומה?
As it is written: 'And you shall bear no sin because of it
when you set apart its best from it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That a separation done the wrong way (bad for good) still makes real תרומה.

steps.title: Why a sin proves the תרומה works
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי explains that a sin could only exist if the separation took effect, so the bad produce really is תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it does not become holy, why would there be a sin? From here we learn that if someone separates from the bad for the good, his תרומה is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעאי finishes his proof by explaining the logic of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the separation did nothing, he did nothing wrong, so there would be no sin. Since the פסוק talks about a sin, the separation must have worked. The same applies to impure produce: it is real תרומה by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy (here, it takes on the status of תרומה)
Carrying a sin
From here (we learn)

steps.whatToRemember: Separating תרומה the wrong way (bad for good, or impure for pure) still creates real תרומה by Torah law. You can only sin by an act that actually takes effect.

phrases.english: And if it does not become holy,
why would there be a bearing of sin?

phrases.aramaic: מִיכָּן לַתּוֹרֵם מִן הָרָעָה עַל הַיָּפָה —
phrases.english: From here we learn that one who separates from the bad for the good,
his תרומה is תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק in step 3 proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: That the separated bad (or impure) produce is real תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that a sin requires an act that took effect.

steps.title: רבה challenges רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks רב חסדא how the רבנן could turn Torah-level תרומה back into ordinary food just because the person might be careless.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to רב חסדא: You said he did nothing at all, so that even the se'ah he separated goes back to being טבל. What is the reason? It is a גזירה, in case he is careless and does not separate again. But is there anything that is תרומה by Torah law, and the רבנן made it ordinary food because he might be careless? Can a בית דין make a rule that uproots something from the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: Using רבי אלעאי's teaching, רבה now attacks רב חסדא's view that the separated portion goes back to being טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said even the separated portion is not תרומה. His reason is a rabbinic גזירה, so the person will not rely on it and skip separating again. But we just showed it is real תרומה by Torah law. How can the רבנן cancel a Torah status? That would be uprooting a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you
A se'ah (a measure of produce), here the portion he separated
Its טבל state (produce not yet tithed)
A protective decree of the רבנן
He is careless or negligent
To uproot something from the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This raises the big question of whether the רבנן have the power to cancel a Torah-level status. That is a major theme of this part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: רבה said to רב חסדא:
According to you, who said

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְּלוּם כׇּל עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: he has done nothing at all,
meaning that even that se'ah returns to its untithed state,
what is the reason?
It is a decree, in case he is careless and does not separate again.

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הָוֵי תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: Is there anything that by Torah law is תרומה,
and because he might be careless,
the רבנן turned it into ordinary food?
And can a court make a rule
to uproot something from the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה לְרַב חִסְדָּא: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of steps 2-4 (it is Torah-level תרומה) to challenge רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that even the separated se'ah goes back to being טבל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the portion is real תרומה by Torah law, a rabbinic גזירה that makes it ordinary food would uproot a Torah law, which a בית דין supposedly cannot do.

steps.title: רב חסדא points to the child who is called a ממזר from the first husband
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רבה that he must also accept that חכמים can uproot Torah law. The proof is the משנה that calls the first husband's child a ממזר, which seems to let him marry a ממזרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Don't you hold this too? We learned that the child is a ממזר from both men. From the second man, fine. But why from the first? She is his wife, so the child is a full Jew, yet we let him marry a ממזרת!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers רבה's question by showing that a משנה already seems to let חכמים override Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, the first husband's child is a kosher Jew and may not marry a ממזרת. If the חכמים call him a ממזר, they seem to permit him to marry a ממזרת. That would be uprooting a Torah prohibition, and not just adding a stringency.

keyTerms.meaning: And you, don't you hold this too?
A child born from a forbidden union, such as adultery
A female ממזר
A full, kosher Jew
Granted, this part makes sense

phrases.english: He said to him: And you, do you not hold so?
phrases.notes: רב חסדא is answering רבה here. He means that רבה also has to agree that חכמים can do this.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: The child is a mamzer from this one and from that one.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about a woman who remarried after hearing her husband died, and then the first husband came back.

phrases.english: Granted, from the second man he is a mamzer
but from the first husband, why?
She is his wife, and the child is a full-fledged Jew,
and yet we permit him to marry a mamzeret!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרַא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge by citing the משנה (הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה), which seems to show that חכמים can uproot a Torah law
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין can uproot a Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that calls the first husband's child a ממזר

steps.title: רבה answers that the child is only stricter, not permitted to a ממזרת
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes שמואל and רבי יוחנן: the first husband's child is still forbidden to marry a ממזרת. Calling him a ממזר only adds a stringency, so that he may not marry a regular Jewish woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: שמואל said he is forbidden to a ממזרת. When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן that he is forbidden to a ממזרת. So why is he called a ממזר? To forbid him to a Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on רב חסדא's proof. The ממזר label in that משנה only makes things stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two great authorities rule that the first husband's child is forbidden to a ממזרת, so the Torah law stays in place. The חכמים only added an extra prohibition on marrying a בת ישראל. Adding a stringency is not the same as uprooting a Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing its teachings
To forbid him
A regular Jewish woman

steps.confusionAlert: The child is not a real ממזר here. He has the strictness of both sides: he may not marry a ממזרת, and he may not marry a regular Jewish woman.

phrases.english: He said to him, Shmuel said as follows:
He is forbidden to marry a mamzeret.
And similarly, when Ravin came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said: He is forbidden to marry a mamzeret.
So why does the Mishnah call him a "mamzer"?
To forbid him to marry a Jewish woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ממזר case completely
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the child may marry a ממזרת. In fact he is forbidden to, so no Torah law was uprooted.

steps.title: רב חסדא sends a new proof about inheriting a minor wife
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא sends a ברייתא to רבה. It says a husband inherits his minor wife, becomes impure for her, and lets her eat תרומה, even though the marriage works only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא sent this to רבה through רב אחא בר רב הונא: Can't בית דין set up a rule that uproots something from the Torah? A ברייתא teaches: From when does a man inherit his minor wife? בית שמאי say: from when she grows up. בית הלל say: from when she enters the חופה. רבי אליעזר says: from when they have relations. Then he inherits her, becomes impure for her, and she eats תרומה because of him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tries again with a stronger proof that בית דין can uproot Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטנה married off by her mother or brother is married only by rabbinic decree. By Torah law, her property should go to her father's family. Yet the ברייתא gives the husband her inheritance, and he may become impure for her as a כהן. That seems to override Torah rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Make a stipulation or set up a rule
To uproot something from the Torah
A girl under the age of maturity
The wedding canopy, which completes the marriage
He becomes impure for her, even as a כהן, when she dies

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main test case for whether a rabbinic marriage can override Torah-level rules of inheritance and טומאה.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda sent to Rabba

phrases.aramaic: בְּיַד רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: by way of Rav Acha bar Rav Huna:
And can the court not stipulate
to uproot something from the Torah?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: מֵאֵימָתַי אָדָם יוֹרֵשׁ אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ קְטַנָּה?
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: From when does a man inherit his minor wife?
phrases.notes: She was married off by her mother or brother, so the marriage counts only מדרבנן, not by Torah law.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: From when she stands at her full height,
phrases.notes: "Stands at her height" means she has grown up and reached maturity.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: From when she enters the wedding canopy,
Rabbi Eliezer says: From when she has relations with him.
And he inherits her, and becomes impure for her,
and she eats teruma on his account.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַבָּה בְּיַד רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof, offered after the first one was rejected
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין can uproot a Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a husband inheriting his minor wife

steps.title: Does בית שמאי really not require the חופה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to question בית שמאי's opinion. It sounds as if growing up alone is enough for him to inherit her, even without a חופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: from when she grows up. Even if she has not entered the חופה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to clarify a detail in the ברייתא before using it as a proof. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with an adult woman, אירוסין alone does not let the husband inherit her. So it is hard to believe that a minor who simply grew up, without any חופה, would be inherited.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
She entered the wedding canopy

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: From when she stands at her full height.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא נִכְנְסָה לַחוּפָּה?
phrases.english: Even though she has not entered the wedding canopy?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא נִכְנְסָה לַחוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of בית שמאי in the ברייתא just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's opinion in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Growing up alone, without a חופה, cannot be enough to inherit a wife when even an adult ארוסה is not inherited.

steps.title: בית שמאי require both growing up and the חופה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads בית שמאי: she must grow up and also enter the חופה. בית שמאי are telling בית הלל that a חופה works only if she has already grown up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: from when she grows up and enters the חופה. This is what בית שמאי told בית הלל: You said 'from when she enters the חופה.' If she has grown up, the חופה works for her. If not, the חופה does not work for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining that בית שמאי agree a חופה is needed. They only add that she must be grown up for it to count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי and בית הלל both require a חופה. The argument is whether a חופה done while she is still a minor works. For בית שמאי, it works only if she has matured.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; read it this way
It works or takes effect

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי require a חופה after she has grown up. בית הלל let the חופה work even while she is a minor.

phrases.english: Say: From when she stands at her full height and enters the wedding canopy.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכִי קָאָמְרוּ לֵיהּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל:
phrases.english: And this is what Beit Shammai were saying to Beit Hillel:
That which you said, from when she enters the wedding canopy:

phrases.aramaic: אִי עָמְדָה בְּקוֹמָתָהּ — מַהְנְיָא לַהּ חוּפָּה,
phrases.english: if she has grown to her full height, the canopy works for her,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לָא מַהְנְיָא לַהּ חוּפָּה.
phrases.english: and if not, the canopy does not work for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of בית שמאי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי hold that growing up alone, without a חופה, is enough
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי require a חופה too, but only one done after she has matured counts

steps.title: How can רבי אליעזר say the husband inherits after relations with a minor?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר: the husband inherits her once they have relations. The גמרא asks how that fits with his own rule that a minor girl's actions mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: from when she has relations. But רבי אליעזר himself said that the actions of a minor girl are nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps checking the wording of the ברייתא, now for רבי אליעזר's view. It points out that his view here seems to clash with another rule he taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, רבי אליעזר says relations alone, even while she is still a minor, give the husband the right to inherit her. But elsewhere רבי אליעזר rules that nothing a קטנה does has any legal effect. If her actions mean nothing, relations with her as a minor should not count either.

keyTerms.meaning: From when she has marital relations
The actions of a minor girl
Are nothing, they have no legal effect

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: from when she has relations.
But didn't Rabbi Eliezer say:
The actions of a minor girl are nothing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of wording question as Step 9, now aimed at רבי אליעזר instead of בית שמאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's statement in the ברייתא that the husband inherits from when they have relations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר holds that a minor's actions have no effect, so relations while she is a minor should not give the husband any rights.

steps.title: She must grow up and also have relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי אליעזר: the husband inherits once she has grown up and they have relations as an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: from when she grows up and has relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading רבי אליעזר's words. He means relations after she has already grown up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations while she is still a קטנה do nothing, which fits his rule. Once she is grown, relations work as a real act of marriage, and only then does the husband inherit her. This follows the same pattern as the answer for בית שמאי in Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, read it this way
From when she grows up

phrases.english: Say: from when she grows up and has relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11 by rereading רבי אליעזר's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר meant relations even while she is a minor.
steps.terutzMaskana: He means relations after she has grown up, so his rule that a minor's actions mean nothing stays true.

steps.title: Back to the proof: the husband inherits only מדרבנן
steps.stepSummary: Returning to רב חסדא's proof: by Torah law her father's family inherits her, yet מדרבנן the husband inherits her. So חכמים seem to uproot Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches that he inherits her. But here, by Torah law her father's family inherits her, and only by rabbinic law does the husband inherit her!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the wording side questions are settled, the גמרא goes back to the main point of the ברייתא from Step 8. It presses the proof that חכמים can uproot a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor orphan's marriage works only מדרבנן, so by Torah law she has no husband, and her father's family should inherit her. Still, the ברייתא says the husband inherits. That looks like חכמים taking away a Torah right of inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event it teaches, the part that matters for our question
He inherits her
By Torah law
By rabbinic law

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches that he inherits her.
But here,
where by Torah law her father inherits her,
phrases.notes: Her father has died, so 'her father' here means his family, who are her heirs by Torah law.

phrases.english: and by rabbinic law the husband inherits her?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back past the wording side questions (Steps 9 to 12) to the proof רב חסדא sent in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים can uproot a Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that the husband inherits his minor wife, whose marriage is only מדרבנן

steps.title: בית דין can declare property ownerless
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside: in money matters, what בית דין declares ownerless becomes ownerless, so they may give her property to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Property declared ownerless by בית דין is ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside רב חסדא's proof with a short, well-known rule. Money is a special area where חכמים have real power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים are not uprooting a Torah law here. בית דין has the power to take property away from its owner, so they can take the inheritance from her father's family and hand it to the husband. This answer works only for money matters, not for other kinds of איסורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that בית דין declares ownerless becomes ownerless

steps.whatToRemember: Inheritance is a money matter. Because of הפקר בית דין הפקר, חכמים can move property from one person to another, so this case does not show that they can uproot other Torah laws.
steps.whyThisMatters: הפקר בית דין הפקר is a basic rule used all over ש״ס to explain how rabbinic rules can change who owns money.

phrases.english: Property declared ownerless by the court is ownerless.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of Step 13 by showing that money matters are different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the proof to money matters only
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed חכמים were uprooting Torah law, but in money matters בית דין simply has the power to transfer ownership.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's source from the פסוק in עזרא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק brings a פסוק showing that the leaders could take away a person's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said: Where do we learn that property declared ownerless by בית דין is ownerless? From the פסוק: "Whoever does not come within three days, by the advice of the princes and the elders, all his property will be forfeited, and he will be separated from the community of the exile."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the rule of Step 14. רבי יצחק learns it from a פסוק in עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עזרא, the leaders warned that anyone who did not come would lose all his property. If leaders can take away a person's property, then בית דין can declare property ownerless.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we learn it?
Will be forfeited, taken away
His property

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that property declared ownerless by the court is ownerless?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָבֹא לִשְׁלֹשֶׁת הַיָּמִים
phrases.english: As it says: "Whoever does not come within three days,
by the advice of the princes and the elders,
all his property will be forfeited,
and he will be separated from the community of the exile."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהֶפְקֵר בֵּית דִּין הֶפְקֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the rule used in Step 14.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא 10:8, where the leaders could take away a person's property

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source from the פסוק in יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns the same rule from the words "heads of the fathers": just as fathers can pass their property to their sons however they want, leaders can give property to the people however they want.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said, from here: "These are the inheritances that אלעזר the כהן, יהושע בן נון, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of בני ישראל gave out." What do heads have to do with fathers? It comes to teach you: just as fathers pass to their sons whatever they want, so too heads, the leaders, give the people whatever they want.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different source for the same rule. רבי אלעזר finds it in a strange phrase in a פסוק in יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "heads of the fathers" puts two words side by side that seem unrelated. רבי אלעזר explains that the פסוק is comparing them: a father may divide his property among his sons as he chooses, and leaders may likewise divide property among the people as they choose. That is the power of הפקר בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, from this source
Heads of the fathers, the tribal leaders
What does this have to do with
Give as an inheritance, pass down property

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for הפקר בית דין הפקר: רבי יצחק learns it from the פסוק in עזרא, and רבי אלעזר learns it from the comparison of leaders to fathers in יהושע.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said, from here:
"These are the inheritances that were given out by
Elazar the priest and Yehoshua son of Nun
and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Israel."

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה עִנְיַן רָאשִׁים אֵצֶל אָבוֹת?
phrases.english: What do heads have to do with fathers?
Rather, it is to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אָבוֹת מַנְחִילִין בְּנֵיהֶם כׇּל מַה שֶּׁיִּרְצוּ —
phrases.english: Just as fathers give their sons as an inheritance whatever they want,

phrases.aramaic: אַף רָאשִׁים מַנְחִילִין אֶת הָעָם כׇּל מַה שֶּׁיִּרְצוּ.
phrases.english: so too heads give the people as an inheritance whatever they want.
phrases.notes: 'Heads' means the leaders and judges of the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the same rule that רבי יצחק learned in Step 15.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהושע 19:51, comparing the leaders to fathers who pass property to their sons as they wish

steps.title: The husband becomes impure for her, against Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא's proof continues with another line of the ברייתא. The husband becomes impure for her, even though by Torah law only her father's side would do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says the husband becomes impure for her. But here, by Torah law her father becomes impure for her, and only by rabbinic law does the husband become impure for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes one more ruling from the ברייתא: the husband becomes impure for her funeral. It uses this ruling as more proof that חכמים can uproot Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may only become impure for close relatives, including his wife. By Torah law this girl is not really his wife, so she still belongs to her father's family. If חכמים let the husband, even a כהן, become impure for her, they seem to permit a Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: becomes ritually impure, here by attending to a dead body
by Torah law
by rabbinic law
husband

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a stronger form of רב חסדא's proof than the inheritance case. Becoming impure is a ritual prohibition, not a money matter, so the answer from Step 14 (בית דין can declare property ownerless) does not work here.

phrases.english: And he becomes impure for her.
phrases.notes: We're back to the ברייתא: the husband of a girl married as a minor, even a כהן, takes care of her burial.

phrases.english: But here is a case
where by Torah law her father becomes impure for her,
and by rabbinic law the husband becomes impure for her!
phrases.notes: By Torah law she isn't his wife, so a כהן husband should not be allowed to become impure for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא אָבִיהָ מִיטַּמֵּא לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the money case was answered, the גמרא brings a second clause from the same ברייתא, this time about ritual impurity.
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים can uproot a Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that the husband of a minor, even a כהן, becomes impure for her

steps.title: She counts as a corpse with no one to bury her
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside. The husband may become impure for her because she counts as a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is because she is a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב חסדא's proof. The husband is not breaking a Torah law, because she has the status of a מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a כהן, and even a כהן גדול, must become impure to bury a מת מצוה, a body no one else will bury. If the girl has that status, the Torah itself permits the husband to bury her. So חכמים are not uprooting anything.

keyTerms.meaning: a dead body with no one to bury it; anyone, even a כהן, must bury it
because

phrases.english: Because she is a corpse with no one to bury it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 17 by giving a Torah-level reason for the husband's impurity.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the impurity case. It does not decide the general question of whether חכמים can uproot Torah law.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the husband has no Torah permission. In fact the Torah allows a כהן to become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.title: But she has family who could bury her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. A ברייתא defines a מת מצוה as one with no one to bury it, and this girl has her father's family.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is she really a מת מצוה? But a ברייתא teaches: What is a מת מצוה? Any body that has no one to bury it. If someone calls out and others answer, that is not a מת מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 18. It brings a ברייתא showing that a body is only a מת מצוה if no one will come to bury it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This girl has relatives, her father's family. If someone called out for them, they could come and bury her. By the ברייתא's definition, then, she should not count as a מת מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: people to bury
one calls out and others answer

phrases.english: And is she a מת מצוה?
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected spelling of the word.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Which is a מת מצוה?
Any body that has no one to bury it.
If one calls out and others answer him,
this is not a מת מצוה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in Step 18 that she counts as a מת מצוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the girl counts as a מת מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מת מצוה must have no one to answer a call for burial. This girl has her father's family, so she does not fit the definition.

steps.title: Her family will not answer since they do not inherit her
steps.stepSummary: Since her father's family does not inherit her, they would not come when called, so she has no one else to bury her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, since they do not inherit her, she calls out and they do not answer her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the answer that she is a מת מצוה. Her father's family gets nothing from her estate, so in practice they will not bother to bury her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's test is whether people will actually answer, not only whether relatives exist. Since the husband inherits her by rabbinic law, her father's family has no interest in caring for her. That leaves only the husband, so for him she counts as a מת מצוה, and the Torah allows him to become impure for her.

keyTerms.meaning: they inherit
here too (applies the rule to this case)
she calls out and they do not answer

steps.whatToRemember: The impurity case does not prove that חכמים uproot Torah law. Because her father's family does not inherit her, they will not bury her. That makes her a מת מצוה, and the Torah itself lets even a כהן become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.confusionAlert: The girl does have living relatives. She counts as a מת מצוה because they will not actually come, not because nobody exists. The ברייתא's test is whether anyone answers the call.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא יָרְתִי לַהּ —
phrases.english: Here too, since they do not inherit her,
phrases.notes: "They" means her father's family. The husband inherits her instead.

phrases.english: she calls out and they do not answer her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא יָרְתִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 19 by showing the girl does fit the ברייתא's definition of a מת מצוה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies the definition to this case: having relatives is not enough if they will not answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since she has a father's family, someone would answer the call, so she is not a מת מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her father's family does not inherit her, so they will not answer. She is a מת מצוה, and the husband may become impure for her by Torah law.
